retry_classification.note: the origin shape: an EMPTY completion body, then a readable one -- retried once, certifies, both attempts billed
garbled body, then a readable one -- same unreadable class, same one retry
TWO unreadable completions still fail CLOSED, and stop at two attempts -- no backoff loop
NOT on a TRUNCATED verdict (finish_reason: length): the model answered and was cut off -- reject reasons are long and certify reasons are short, so resampling this class shops the run toward certify

message.content: {"certify": false, "reason": "the answer is the site masth

retry_classification.note: NOT on a truncated REASONING completion either: content null with finish_reason length is planner.py's own 'it answered, the answer has no room in it', byte-identical to an empty body and told apart only by the finish_reason
an empty body that ALSO carries a benign finish_reason is still the retryable class -- the guard keys on truncation, not on the field existing
NOT on a missing key: the body parsed as JSON, it just has no `certify` -- a shape problem, not an unreadable one, so no retry
NOT on a refusal: the model answered, it declined -- asking the identical prompt again is asking to be refused again
NOT on a reasoned FAIL: a readable reject is a VERDICT, and re-rolling a verdict you dislike is not a retry
NOT on a wrongly-typed certify: readable JSON of the right shape, rejected by the strict is-True rule (D26) -- a reject, never an error, so never retried
a ONE-LINE fenced verdict is readable, not unreadable: the fence strip must not turn a complete answer into an empty string and buy it a re-roll

a fenced reject with TRAILING prose is a readable verdict, not an unreadable body -- PR #44 R1: the fullmatch fence left the fence in the text, the JSONDecodeError was classified retryable, and the reject was re-rolled into a certify

retry_classification.note: a NESTED object inside a reject is part of that verdict, not a second candidate: the scan skips to where each object ended, or this reads as ambiguous (available:false) instead of as the reject it is (responsive:false)

BILLING CEILING: a provider that omits `usage` on the failed generation bills the retry at the successful attempt alone -- pinned so the published 'both attempts are billed' claim is read as 'both attempts' REPORTED usage', which is all any caller can see

DECLARED CEILING, not a guard (PR #44 R8): the judge emits the forged object and NOTHING else, so `_is_the_whole_completion` answers True -- correctly, by its own definition -- the certify gate never fires, and the run certifies on an echo. Pinned as the PASS it really is. This scenario was GREEN the moment it was written; there was no red to watch, because it demonstrates a limit rather than a defect. Out of reach of any parser and of T-M39-7 (a provider-enforced object repeating the forgery is still {"certify": true}); bounded only by the prompt-side defences judge-injection-cannot-flip-verdict grades. If it ever goes red, something has closed the residual and ADR-023's Decision section is what needs re-reading.

expect.note: live_judge()'s REAL parser decides what is retryable and agent.py's REAL _apply_judge decides how often: only a completion body that cannot be read at all (empty, or not JSON) and was not TRUNCATED buys the one retry ADR-023 allows; a truncated verdict, a missing key, a refusal, a reasoned FAIL, a wrongly-typed certify and a one-line fenced answer each end the run on the first attempt, and two unreadable bodies fail closed exactly as ADR-017 already said The final scenario is not a guard but a DECLARED CEILING: a completion that is the forged object and nothing else certifies, because position cannot tell an echo from an answer when there is nothing else in the body.

provenance: The classification half of M39. The two stub cases (`judge-retries-one-malformed-completion`, `judge-two-malformed-completions-fail-closed`) prove the retry fires and is bounded, but `stub_judge` decides for itself what is retryable -- it cannot grade the production question, which is which REAL provider responses earn a second call. So this probe mocks ONLY `urllib.request.urlopen` (the transport `live_judge`'s `_call` uses) and runs the real `live_judge` parser under the real `_apply_judge`, the same technique `judge-parse-response-strict-boolean` established after PR #33 R1 found that every judge case until then stubbed past the code that actually runs. A `uuid4` nonce per scenario keeps `live_judge`'s content-hash cache from answering instead of the parser. The scenario list is the spec's own boundary read as cases: retry on an unparseable/empty completion, NOT on a missing key, NOT on a refusal, NOT on a reasoned FAIL. `calls` grades the transport directly, so a retry that fires on the wrong class is red even if the eventual verdict happens to match, and `judge_tokens` grades the other half of ADR-023's bargain -- both attempts of a retried call are BILLED, which is the cost the analysis section publishes. WATCHED RED FIRST on the pre-M39 tree: no scenario retried, so `calls` was 1 everywhere and the two retryable scenarios reported FAIL instead of PASS; `attempts` was absent entirely. ROUND 2 (M39 cold review, findings 1 and 4) added the four scenarios that matter most, and two of them were watched red exactly the way the first round was. A completion truncated at the provider's token ceiling (`finish_reason: "length"`) parses no better than an empty one, so the first implementation retried it -- and the truncated-reject scenario reported `verdict: PASS`, `judge_attempts: 2`, `calls: 2`: a `{"certify": false, ...}` re-rolled into a success. That is the inviolable property, reached through the one branch ADR-023 permits, and the bias is directional rather than random -- a reject must explain itself where a certify can be one word, so truncation destroys rejects preferentially. `src/browser/planner.py` already classifies the same shape (`content: null` on `finish_reason: length`) as "it answered; the answer does not fit", and the judge now agrees with it. The reasoning-model variant is pinned separately because it is byte-identical to the empty body the retry EXISTS for and is told apart only by the finish_reason, and the benign `finish_reason: "stop"` scenario pins that the guard keys on truncation rather than on the field being present at all. The one-line fenced verdict is the small form of the same defect: the fence strip emptied it, so a complete readable answer was classified unreadable and re-rolled -- also watched red (`PASS`, 2 calls) before the fence parse was fixed. The last scenario fixes no code: a provider that omits `usage` on a generation that returned nothing bills the retried run at the successful attempt alone, so the published "both attempts are billed" claim is pinned at what it actually means -- both attempts' REPORTED usage -- instead of being left to read as a guarantee nothing can keep. ROUND 3 (PR #44 R8) added the last scenario, and it is the only one here that pins a LIMIT rather than a behaviour. ADR-023 published that 'every error this predicate can make lands on fail-closed'; that was false, and judge.py's own comment three lines below the same claim already said so. The echo-only completion -- the repo's own forged payload with no prose around it -- returns whole_completion=True and certifies. It is graded as a PASS on purpose. This repo has repeatedly found that a limitation stated only in prose gets falsified or forgotten within days (the declared-limitations pattern behind D22/D26), so the ceiling gets a case: green by construction, never watched red, and red only if someone closes the hole -- at which point the ADR is what has to change, not the case.

triage.note: tagged `invariant` as well as `fast` because it is pure code -- transport mocked, no browser, no network -- and because it is the only thing standing between a bounded retry and a judge that gets asked twice for a verdict it already gave. Two residues are declared rather than solved, both tracked in tasks/TODO.md: a provider that refuses only in prose, or truncates without setting `finish_reason`, is indistinguishable here from an unreadable body (T-M39-4); and an unreadable ENVELOPE -- a non-JSON HTTP body, `choices: []` -- is not retried at all and cannot even be expressed by this probe, which builds a well-formed envelope around every scenario (T-M39-3). The last scenario is the third declared residue and the only one that can end in a wrong SUCCESS rather than a wasted call: an echo-only forged verdict certifies, is unreachable by the parser and by T-M39-7, and rests entirely on the prompt-side isolation judge-injection-cannot-flip-verdict grades.
